intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Temple Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent 12th-century Khmer temple complex at sunrise, wandering through Angkor Wat, Bayon, and Ta Prohm. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for a full-day guided circuit covering the most iconic temples and learning about the ancient Khmer Empire.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda Visit
experiences.description: Tour the stunning Royal Palace complex and the Silver Pagoda, home to a life-sized gold Buddha studded with diamonds. Combine with a visit to the nearby National Museum to explore Khmer artifacts and sculptures spanning centuries of Cambodian history and culture.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine island of Koh Rong Samloem and spend the day on Saracen Bay's crystal-clear turquoise waters. Snorkel among coral reefs, swim in bioluminescent waters at night, and relax on one of Southeast Asia's most unspoiled white-sand beaches.
experiences.location: Saracen Bay, Koh Rong Samloem, Sihanoukville

experiences.name: Cambodian Street Food and Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening street food walk through the Old Market area, sampling local delicacies such as fish amok, Khmer curry, nom banh chok noodles, and fresh tropical fruit. Visit the bustling Psah Chas night market and interact with local vendors to understand Cambodian culinary traditions.
experiences.location: Old Market (Psah Chas) area, Siem Reap

experiences.name: Killing Fields and Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
experiences.description: Visit the deeply moving Choeung Ek Killing Fields memorial and the Tuol Sleng S-21 Genocide Museum to understand Cambodia's tragic Khmer Rouge history. Audio guides provide powerful personal testimonies, offering profound insight into the resilience of the Cambodian people and their path to reconciliation.
experiences.location: Choeung Ek and Toul Tom Poung district, Phnom Penh

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. After settling in, take a relaxed tuk-tuk ride through Siem Reap town to get oriented. Visit the Siem Reap Art Center Night Market area in the late afternoon to browse local crafts and get a feel for the city.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area for your first evening. Enjoy the lively atmosphere and pick up a cheap local meal from a street stall or a budget restaurant nearby.

meals.breakfast: Eaten before or during flight — skip or grab a snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a local noodle shop near the hotel upon arrival (~$2–3 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Khmer restaurant near Pub Street such as 'Khmer Kitchen' — try amok curry and jasmine rice (~$4–6 USD).

day_by_day.notes: November is the tail end of the rainy season in Cambodia — expect mostly dry, pleasant weather around 28–32°C. Keep small USD bills and Cambodian Riel handy. Tuk-tuks from the airport to Angkor area cost roughly $8–12 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before dawn (4:30 AM) and hire a tuk-tuk to Angkor Wat to witness the iconic sunrise over the temple reflected in the lotus pond. This is one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Hindu epic Mahabharata, and the central towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or cycle to Angkor Thom — the great walled city. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, then explore the Baphuon Temple, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Take a shaded rest during peak heat (12:00–14:00).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Visit the Angkor Night Market for affordable souvenirs. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance — some budget restaurants offer free shows with dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early morning — pack a banana and water or grab a $1 baguette from a street vendor near Angkor Wat entrance.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local stall near Angkor Thom — rice with pork or grilled chicken (~$2–3 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Bugs Cafe' or a local Khmer BBQ restaurant near Old Market (~$5–7 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Archaeological Park pass ($62 USD) — it covers today and the next two days of temple visits. Rent a bicycle from your guesthouse for ~$2–3/day to explore independently. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the jungle temple of Ta Prohm — famously known as the 'Tomb Raider temple' — where massive silk-cotton tree roots engulf ancient stone walls. Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Continue to Banteay Kdei, a quieter Buddhist monastery temple nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Srah Srang — a royal bathing pool with beautiful lakeside views. Then cycle or tuk-tuk to Pre Rup, a 10th-century state temple-mountain with panoramic views of the surrounding jungle — perfect for afternoon light photography.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Siem Reap. Visit the Cambodian Cultural Village (budget entry ~$5 USD) for a condensed cultural experience, or simply relax at a local café. Try a traditional Khmer massage for ~$7–10 USD.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or a local café — Khmer rice porridge (Bobor) (~$1.50–2 USD).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Srah Srang — buy fresh fruit, baguettes, and water from roadside vendors (~$2 USD).
meals.dinner: Try 'Mahob Restaurant' or a local family-run eatery — fish amok and sticky rice (~$5–6 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm gets crowded midday — arrive early. Wear modest clothing (shoulders and knees covered) as a sign of respect at all temple sites. Stay hydrated — November days can still be warm and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Use your 3-day Angkor pass for the final day. Head to the outer Angkor circuit — visit Preah Khan, a sprawling flat temple complex dedicated to Jayavarman VII's father, filled with long corridors and intricate carvings. Then visit Neak Pean, a unique artificial island temple surrounded by water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ta Som — a small but beautifully preserved temple with a famous tree-engulfed eastern gopura. Finish at East Mebon, a temple-mountain originally surrounded by water from the East Baray reservoir. Spend some time at the massive East Baray reservoir viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Angkor temples with a sunset at Phnom Bakheng hill — a short climb offers sweeping views over the jungle and Angkor Wat silhouette at dusk. Return to town for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Local café near guesthouse — fried rice with egg (~$2 USD).
meals.lunch: Street food near Preah Khan — grilled corn, fresh coconut, and spring rolls (~$2–3 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Khmer buffet restaurant — all-you-can-eat for ~$5–7 USD including traditional dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Bakheng sunset is popular — arrive 30–45 minutes early as visitor numbers are capped. Wear comfortable shoes for the hill climb. This is the last day of your Angkor pass — make the most of it.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to the floating villages of Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Hire a boat tour (~$10–15 USD) to see the extraordinary stilted and floating communities of Kampong Phluk or Chong Kneas, where entire villages float on the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor Centre for Conservation of Biodiversity (ACCB) — a free or low-cost wildlife sanctuary near Siem Reap that rescues and rehabilitates endangered Cambodian wildlife including gibbons and birds. Alternatively, visit the Landmine Museum (~$5 USD) to learn about Cambodia's tragic history with landmines.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Siem Reap's local market scene — visit Psar Leu (the local market away from tourists) for authentic Cambodian goods at local prices. Enjoy street food for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café — Khmer crepes (Banh Chao) with coffee (~$2 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat on the boat tour or at a floating village restaurant — fresh lake fish with rice (~$3–4 USD).
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Psar Leu market — grilled skewers, noodle soup, and fresh fruit (~$3 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap boat tours vary in price — negotiate and compare options. November water levels are still high, making it an excellent time to visit. Bring insect repellent for the lake area.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a budget bus or shared minivan from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 5–6 hours, ~$6–10 USD). Book with Giant Ibis, Mekong Express, or Larryta for reliable service. Enjoy the Cambodian countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh early afternoon. Check into a budget guesthouse in the BKK1 or Riverside area (~$8–15/night). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the stunning royal residence with gleaming spires and a pagoda floor made of 5,000 silver tiles (~$10 USD entry).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Phnom Penh Riverside promenade (Sisowath Quay) as the sun sets over the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers. Browse the Night Market (Phsar Reatrey) along the riverside for food and crafts.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before bus departure — rice soup or baguette with pâté (~$1.50 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat on the bus or at a roadside stop — packed lunch or local noodles (~$2–3 USD).
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh — try lok lak (Cambodian beef stir-fry) with rice (~$4–6 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus ticket 1 day in advance, especially during peak season. Phnom Penh is a larger, busier city — be aware of your belongings, especially on the riverside. Tuk-tuks within the city cost $2–4 USD per trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply important and sobering historical site that was a Khmer Rouge prison during the 1975–1979 genocide. Entry ~$5 USD. This is a profoundly moving experience that provides essential context for understanding modern Cambodia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields (~$6 USD entry) located about 15 km outside the city — hire a tuk-tuk for ~$10 round trip. The memorial stupa and audio guide provide a powerful and respectful commemoration of the victims. Afterward, decompress with a visit to the nearby peaceful Wat Phnom — the city's founding temple.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building from 1937 selling everything from jewelry to street food. Enjoy a quiet evening meal and reflect on the day's history.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café — baguette with cheese and iced coffee (~$2 USD).
meals.lunch: Local Khmer restaurant near Tuol Sleng — rice and vegetable curry (~$3 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant near Central Market — Khmer noodle soup (Kuy Teav) and fresh juice (~$4 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek are emotionally heavy experiences — take your time and be respectful. Dress modestly. It is recommended to hire an audio guide at Choeung Ek ($3 USD) for deeper understanding. Allow time to process these experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Museum of Cambodia — a beautiful terracotta building housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture, including pieces from Angkor (~$5 USD entry). Then visit the nearby Wat Ounalom — the headquarters of Cambodian Buddhism, a working monastery with monks in residence.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Take a budget bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Kampot (~3–4 hours, ~$6–8 USD). Kampot is a charming riverside colonial town near the southern coast. Check into a budget guesthouse (~$8–12/night). Explore the French colonial architecture of Kampot's Old Town on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cruise on the Kampot River — many guesthouses and tour operators offer cheap boat trips (~$5–8 USD) with views of the Bokor Mountain silhouette. Have dinner at a riverside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Local café in Phnom Penh — Khmer pancakes with palm sugar and coconut (~$2 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat during bus stop or upon arrival in Kampot — local noodle shop (~$2–3 USD).
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Kampot — fresh pepper crab or grilled fish (Kampot is famous for its black pepper) (~$5–7 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is famous for its world-renowned Kampot pepper — try to incorporate it into meals. The town is very walkable and bicycle-friendly. November weather in Kampot should be dry and pleasant (~28–30°C).

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~$3–7/day) and ride to Bokor National Park. Visit the eerie abandoned French hill station on the plateau — including the old Bokor Palace Hotel, a Catholic church, and a casino, all frozen in time with misty jungle views. The drive up offers spectacular scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head south to Kep — a small, charming seaside town about 25 km from Kampot (tuk-tuk ~$8–10 return). Visit the famous Kep Crab Market and walk along the Kep Beach promenade. The beach is modest but peaceful, with views of offshore islands. Swim or relax on the quiet shore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot for the evening. Explore the local bar scene along the riverside — many offer cheap happy hour drinks. Enjoy a final evening in this laid-back town.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café in Kampot — eggs, baguette, and Cambodian iced coffee (~$2–3 USD).
meals.lunch: Fresh crab at Kep Crab Market — buy directly from the market vendors and have it cooked with Kampot pepper (~$5–8 USD).
meals.dinner: Local Khmer restaurant in Kampot — fish amok and stir-fried vegetables with rice (~$4–5 USD).

day_by_day.notes: The Bokor Mountain road can be foggy — go in the morning for clearer views. Kep is a great introduction to Cambodia's quieter coastal scene. If you want to extend beach time, consider staying a night in Kep instead.

day_by_day.morning: Optional early morning: Kayak or take a boat trip through the Kampot mangroves — a serene and beautiful ecosystem teeming with birds and wildlife (~$10–15 USD for a guided tour). Alternatively, rent a bicycle and explore the quiet countryside roads around Kampot at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping in Kampot's Old Town — pick up Kampot pepper, handmade crafts, and locally made goods. Take a final relaxed lunch by the river. Depending on your onward travel plans, arrange a bus or shared taxi back to Phnom Penh (~$6–8 USD) for an evening flight, or extend your stay.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Kampot or Phnom Penh — celebrate your 10-day Cambodian adventure with a proper Khmer feast. Reflect on the temples, history, culture, and coast you've experienced.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast in Kampot — fresh fruit platter, yogurt, and local coffee (~$2–3 USD).
meals.lunch: Riverside café lunch in Kampot — baguette sandwich with local fillings and fresh lime juice (~$3 USD).
meals.dinner: Farewell Khmer dinner — a full spread of amok, lok lak, spring rolls, and mango sticky rice (~$7–10 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 10 days: Accommodation ~$80–120, Transport ~$50–70, Food ~$60–80, Entrance fees ~$90–100 (including Angkor pass), Activities ~$40–60 — Total approximately $320–430 USD for 10 days. Always carry small USD bills and negotiate tuk-tuk fares in advance. Cambodia is generally very safe for budget travelers — enjoy every moment!

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel near Angkor Archaeological Park. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around the hotel neighborhood. Visit the nearby Angkor Wat outer grounds (western causeway and reflection pond) for a first glimpse of the iconic temple silhouette without entering — perfect for jet-lag recovery and golden-hour photography.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Siem Reap's Pub Street area and the Old Market (Psah Chas) for a lively introduction to the city. Browse handicrafts and street stalls, then enjoy dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light meal at hotel or a nearby café such as The Little Red Fox Espresso — sandwiches, salads, and fresh juices (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Mahob Restaurant on Pub Street — authentic Khmer cuisine in a mid-range setting; try amok fish curry and lok lak beef (~$12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Buy a 3-day Angkor Pass tomorrow morning at the ticket office (opens 05:00). Stay hydrated — November is warm (~28–32°C) but manageable. Exchange currency or withdraw KHR/USD at airport ATM.

day_by_day.morning: Early start (05:30) to catch sunrise at Angkor Wat. Arrive before dawn and position yourself at the reflecting pools on the western causeway. After sunrise, explore the main temple complex — galleries of bas-reliefs (Battle of Kurukshetra, Heaven and Hell), inner sanctuary, and central towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom — enter through the South Gate with its giant face towers, visit the Bayon Temple (famous for 216 serene stone faces), the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Return to hotel for a midday rest (12:30–14:30).
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ta Prohm temple (the 'Tomb Raider' temple) in the late afternoon light — massive silk-cotton trees growing through ancient stone walls create an unforgettable atmosphere. Return to town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early snack/coffee from a hotel breakfast box or roadside vendor near Angkor Wat (~$2–4)
meals.lunch: Angkor Café (near Angkor Wat ticket area) — Khmer noodles, rice dishes, and smoothies (~$7–12)
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak — award-winning modern Khmer tasting menu (book ahead); a splurge-worthy mid-range treat (~$25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your 3-day Angkor Archaeological Park pass today if not done yesterday (~$62 USD). Wear comfortable walking shoes, sunscreen, and a hat. Carry at least 1.5L of water. Respectful dress code required at all temples (shoulders and knees covered).

day_by_day.morning: Explore the 'Small Circuit' temples — begin with Banteay Kdei (a Buddhist monastery with intricate carvings), then Srah Srang (a royal bathing pool with beautiful morning light reflections). Continue to Prasat Kravan, notable for its rare brick bas-reliefs of Vishnu.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pre Rup (a 10th-century state temple with panoramic views from its towers) and East Mebon (temple-island in the former East Baray reservoir). Rent a bicycle or hire a tuk-tuk for this circuit (~$15–20 for a full-day tuk-tuk).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance at Koulen II Restaurant or Angkor Village Theatre — a beautifully costumed show depicting Khmer mythology. Dinner included at the venue or nearby.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Butterflies Garden Restaurant — fresh fruit, eggs, and Khmer porridge (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Local rice shop near Pre Rup village — rice with grilled meats and vegetables (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Apsara dance dinner show at Angkor Village Theatre (~$18–25 per person including show and set menu)

day_by_day.notes: Day 3 of your Angkor pass. Pace yourself — this is your third consecutive temple day. Consider hiring a licensed local guide (~$25–35/day) for deeper historical context on the Khmer Empire (802–1431 CE).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' located 25km north of Siem Reap. Famous for its extraordinarily detailed pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest in all of Angkor. En route, stop at the landmine museum (CMAC Visitor Center) to learn about Cambodia's tragic recent history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kbal Spean (River of a Thousand Lingas) — a 1.5km jungle hike leads to a riverbed carved with hundreds of Shiva lingas and mythological scenes. Cool, shaded, and far fewer tourists. Return to Siem Reap by 16:00.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique in town — watch skilled craftspeople carve stone, lacquer silk, and create traditional Khmer art. Browse for authentic souvenirs. Stroll the riverside night market for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel or roadside Khmer restaurant near Banteay Srei (~$4–7)
meals.dinner: Malis Restaurant — upscale-casual Khmer dining with recipes inspired by ancient royal cuisine; try the stuffed lemongrass chicken (~$15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk or private car for the Banteay Srei day trip (~$25–35). Bring sturdy shoes for the Kbal Spean hike — the trail can be slippery. The CMAC Landmine Museum is a sobering but essential cultural experience (~$5 entry, supports demining efforts).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tonlé Sap Lake — one of Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lakes and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Take a guided boat tour of the floating villages (Kampong Phluk or Chong Khneas) to see stilted houses, floating schools, and local fishing life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap. Visit the Angkor National Museum for a comprehensive overview of Khmer civilization, art, and religion — excellent context for everything you've seen at the temples (~$12 entry). Spend the remainder of the afternoon relaxing at the hotel pool.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class at Le Tigre de Papier or Cooks in Tuk Tuks — learn to prepare 3–4 traditional Khmer dishes (amok, papaya salad, spring rolls). You'll eat what you cook for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Fresh fish grilled on the boat dock at Tonlé Sap or a lakeside restaurant — local specialty (~$5–9)
meals.dinner: Your own creations at the cooking class (~$25–35 per person including class and dinner)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tonlé Sap boat tour through your hotel or a reputable operator (~$15–20 per person). Choose Kampong Phluk over Chong Khneas for a more authentic, less touristy experience. Book the cooking class in advance as spots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Private taxi or bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (~6 hours by road, or 1-hour flight). Book a morning departure (~07:00–08:00) to maximize afternoon time in the capital. Giant Ibis bus is comfortable and reliable (~$15 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh early afternoon. Check into a mid-range guesthouse in the riverside district (Sisowath Quay area). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — stunning Khmer royal architecture with the famous Emerald Buddha and Pha Bang statue (~$10 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade as the sun sets over the Tonlé Sap/Mekong confluence. Browse the night market (Phsar Reatrey) and enjoy dinner at a riverside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or grab-and-go from a Siem Reap bakery before departure
meals.lunch: Onboard snacks or a stop en route — roadside Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) (~$2–4)
meals.dinner: Romdeng Restaurant, Phnom Penh — social enterprise restaurant serving traditional Cambodian cuisine; try the tarantula fritters if adventurous (~$12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your transport from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh in advance. If flying, book a morning Bassaka Air or Cambodia Angkor Air flight (~$50–80). Pre-arrange accommodation in Phnom Penh before leaving Siem Reap. Store luggage at Siem Reap hotel if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a Khmer Rouge interrogation center. A deeply moving and historically essential experience. Take time to absorb the exhibits and personal testimonies (~$8 entry, audio guide recommended).
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel 15km south to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields — the most significant memorial site of the Khmer Rouge genocide. The audio guide (included in ~$6 entry) is narrated by survivors and is profoundly powerful. Return to Phnom Penh for a reflective rest.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — Southeast Asia's largest archaeological museum, housing the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts (~$10 entry, open until 17:30). Dinner in the BKK1 neighborhood — Phnom Penh's vibrant expat and local dining hub.

meals.breakfast: Café Brown or Java Café, Phnom Penh — excellent coffee, pastries, and full breakfast (~$5–9)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Choeung Ek — simple Khmer rice shop (~$3–5). Keep it simple given the emotional weight of the morning.
meals.dinner: Sla Restaurant (BKK1) — modern Cambodian cuisine with garden seating; try the red tree ant salad or grilled Mekong fish (~$14–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. Dress respectfully (covered shoulders and knees). These sites are critical for understanding modern Cambodian history and the resilience of its people. Consider hiring a survivor guide at Tuol Sleng for a personal account.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco dome built in 1937. Browse gold jewelry, silk scarves, electronics, and fresh produce. Practice bargaining for souvenirs. Then visit the Wat Phnom hilltop temple — the spiritual heart of Phnom Penh with panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Take an afternoon bus or private taxi from Phnom Penh to Kampot (~3 hours, ~$10–15 by bus). Kampot is a charming riverside colonial town and the gateway to Cambodia's southern coast. Check into a riverside guesthouse or boutique hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Kampot River — many guesthouses and tour operators offer 1.5–2 hour sunset boat trips (~$8–12) with views of the Elephant Mountains and fireflies after dark. Dinner in Kampot's relaxed riverside strip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Phnom Penh
meals.lunch: Grab street food near Central Market before departure — bánh mì-style Khmer sandwiches or rice rolls (~$1–3)
meals.dinner: Rikitikitavi Restaurant, Kampot — beloved riverside spot with Khmer and Western fusion; try the Kampot pepper crab or amok (~$10–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is famous for its world-renowned black and red pepper — buy some from a local farm. Book your Kampot guesthouse in advance. The town is small and walkable. Motorbike rentals available (~$5–8/day) for independent exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kep — a sleepy former French colonial beach resort 25km from Kampot. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market (Phsar Kdam) and watch fishermen unload their catch. Walk through the crumbling ruins of French-era villas reclaimed by jungle — a hauntingly beautiful sight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Kep Beach or take a short boat trip to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — a pristine, car-free island with white sand beaches, hammocks strung between palms, and crystal-clear water. Swim, snorkel, and unwind (~$5 return boat trip). Return to Kampot by 17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a Kampot pepper farm on the outskirts of town (La Plantation or Sothy's Pepper Farm) for a guided tour and tasting at golden hour. Return to town for a leisurely dinner along the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Café Espresso or Kampot Coffee — excellent locally grown Cambodian coffee with eggs and toast (~$4–7)
meals.lunch: Fresh steamed crab with Kampot pepper sauce at the Kep Crab Market — the quintessential Cambodian coastal experience (~$8–14)
meals.dinner: Epic Arts Café, Kampot — social enterprise supporting artists with disabilities; wholesome Khmer and Western menu (~$7–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Rabbit Island is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Bring cash as there are no ATMs on the island. Sunscreen and reef-safe products are strongly recommended. November weather on the coast is typically sunny with low humidity — ideal beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Optional early morning visit to Phnom Chhngok Cave Temple — a 5km tuk-tuk ride from Kampot leads to a natural cave containing a 7th-century brick shrine. A short hike with spectacular views and very few tourists (~$2 entry). Alternatively, enjoy a slow final morning at a riverside café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely departure from Kampot. Transfer back to Phnom Penh (~3 hours) for international departure, or to Sihanoukville if you have an onward coastal connection. Use travel time to reflect, journal, and organize purchases. If time allows at Phnom Penh airport, browse duty-free Cambodian rum and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phnom Penh International Airport or overnight stay if flight is the following day. Final dinner at a Phnom Penh airport-area restaurant or in the city if time permits.

meals.breakfast: Final Kampot breakfast at The Greenhouse or a riverside café — fresh fruit bowls, Cambodian iced coffee (~$4–8)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route to Phnom Penh — Khmer noodle soup or rice with grilled pork (~$2–4)
meals.dinner: Phnom Penh airport lounge or a final Khmer meal at Friends Restaurant (Phnom Penh) — another social enterprise training at-risk youth; excellent Cambodian tapas (~$10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure for Phnom Penh airport check-in and security. Confirm your return flight details. Declare any Kampot pepper or food items at customs. Cambodia departure tax is typically included in your ticket. Final currency exchange at airport — spend remaining Riel on snacks or donate to airport charity boxes.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique stay within Angkor Archaeological Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private welcome orientation at the hotel followed by a leisurely poolside refresh. At 15:30, embark on a gentle introductory walk through the outer grounds of Angkor Thom with a private licensed guide — explore the South Gate causeway lined with stone devas and asuras, and admire the Bayon Temple's iconic smiling faces in the warm afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace or rooftop overlooking the jungle canopy. Dinner at a refined Khmer fine-dining restaurant such as Malis Siem Reap or Cuisine Wat Damnak — savoring contemporary interpretations of traditional Cambodian cuisine with curated wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or post-arrival light snack at hotel welcome)
meals.lunch: Elegant welcome lunch at the hotel restaurant upon check-in — fresh Cambodian salads, grilled river fish, and tropical fruit platters
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak or Malis Siem Reap — five-course tasting menu featuring amok, lok lak wagyu beef, and palm sugar desserts paired with Cambodian craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Allow time to acclimatize to the heat and humidity. Confirm guide booking for Day 2 Angkor Wat sunrise visit. Dress modestly for temple visits — shoulders and knees covered.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn departure at 05:00 for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise experience. With a private guide, position at the sacred reflecting pool for the breathtaking moment the sun rises behind the five lotus towers. Explore the outer galleries of Angkor Wat including the extraordinary bas-relief narrative panels depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk and the Hindu epics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-sunrise hotel return for a full breakfast. At 10:30, continue the Angkor complex exploration: visit Ta Prohm — the 'Tomb Raider' temple dramatically engulfed by ancient silk-cotton tree roots — followed by Banteay Kdei. After lunch, rest during peak heat hours (12:30–14:30). At 15:00, explore the Terrace of the Elephants and Terrace of the Leper King within Angkor Thom.
day_by_day.evening: Private Apsara dance performance dinner at a heritage venue such as Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor or a dedicated cultural dinner show. Watch Cambodia's celestial classical dance, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, over a lavish Khmer banquet.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor), freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Upscale lunch at Haven Restaurant or Sugar Palm — Khmer red curry, fresh spring rolls, and coconut-based desserts
meals.dinner: Apsara cultural dinner at Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor or Temple Club — traditional Khmer feast with live classical dance performance

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise visit requires very early departure — set alarms for 04:30. Carry water and sun protection. Angkor Wat entrance is included in the Angkor Pass — purchase a 3-day or 7-day pass for best value. Photography is exceptional at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the remote and less-visited outer Angkor temples: Preah Khan — a vast jungle monastery with atmospheric moss-covered corridors and towering trees — followed by Neak Pean, an island temple set in a sacred pond. These sites offer a more intimate and mystical experience away from the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap town for a curated deep-dive into Khmer civilization, art, and the history of the Angkor Empire. Followed by an exclusive private workshop at a traditional Khmer silk-weaving atelier — learn about the ancient art of hand-loom silk production and browse premium silk scarves and textiles for purchase.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails and tapas at a rooftop bar in Siem Reap's Pub Street area (Asana Wooden House or similar). Dinner at a premium international restaurant such as Embassy Restaurant or a private chef's table experience arranged through the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Continental and Asian breakfast buffet at the hotel
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch box prepared by the hotel chef — enjoyed in a shaded pavilion near Preah Khan temple
meals.dinner: Embassy Restaurant or private chef's table — contemporary fusion cuisine with Cambodian ingredients, paired with fine French wines

day_by_day.notes: Preah Khan and Neak Pean are included in the Angkor Pass. Bring insect repellent for jungle temple visits. The silk atelier visit can often be arranged through the hotel concierge with a private artisan demonstration.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women' — approximately 35km northeast of Siem Reap. Renowned for its extraordinary pink sandstone carvings considered the finest in all of Angkor, this 10th-century temple is a masterpiece of Khmer decorative art. Private guide provides in-depth narrative on the intricate mythological carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, visit Kbal Spean — the 'River of a Thousand Lingas' — a sacred riverbed carved with Hindu iconography high in the Kulen Hills. A moderate 30-minute jungle hike leads to the cascading stream. Alternatively (for those preferring less hiking), visit Banteay Samré, a beautifully preserved Hindu temple nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Indulge in a signature Khmer spa treatment at the hotel or at Bodia Spa — a 90-minute Cambodian herbal compress massage using local botanicals. Dinner at a luxury riverside setting.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch in the Banteay Srei area or at a local garden restaurant in the countryside
meals.dinner: Mahob Restaurant or Viroth's Restaurant — elegant Cambodian fine dining with garden ambiance and candlelit tables

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a full morning — depart by 07:30 to avoid midday heat and tour groups. The Kbal Spean hike involves uneven terrain — wear sturdy footwear. Spa booking should be made 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise boat excursion on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Glide through the floating villages of Kompong Phluk or Kampong Khleang in a private wooden boat, witnessing the extraordinary stilted houses rising 6–8 meters above the water. Meet local fishing families and observe traditional lake life at dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap. Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and showroom — a social enterprise preserving traditional Khmer crafts including lacquerware, stone carving, and silk painting. Enjoy a private artisan demonstration and browse premium handcrafted souvenirs. Followed by leisure time at the hotel pool.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset dinner cruise on Tonlé Sap Lake (if not done in the morning) or a curated food tour of Siem Reap's Old Market area (Phsar Chas) with a culinary expert — tasting street foods elevated by narrative and context, ending at a premium cocktail bar.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the early lake departure
meals.lunch: Brunch upon return — hotel restaurant or The Sugar Palm for authentic Khmer home cooking
meals.dinner: Private sunset dinner on a chartered lake boat with a catered Khmer menu, or Cuisine Wat Damnak for a second visit with a different seasonal tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap water levels in November are ideal — the lake is at near-full flood season, making floating village access excellent. Bring a light jacket for the early morning boat ride. Artisans Angkor purchases directly support local craftspeople.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh via luxury charter flight or premium domestic flight (approximately 1 hour). Check in to a luxury Phnom Penh hotel such as Rosewood Phnom Penh or Raffles Hotel Le Royal. After settling in, begin exploration with a private guided visit to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — marvel at the Throne Hall, the Emerald Buddha, and the floor of 5,000 silver tiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sobering but essential cultural visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and Choeung Ek Memorial — understanding Cambodia's tragic 20th-century history under the Khmer Rouge is a profound and important part of any meaningful visit. Private guide provides thoughtful, respectful context.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Rosewood Sky Bar or Eclipse Sky Bar — panoramic views over the Mekong and Tonlé Sap confluence. Dinner at a top Phnom Penh restaurant such as Malis Phnom Penh or Topaz Restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Siem Reap before transfer
meals.lunch: Upscale lunch at Khéma La Poste or Friends Restaurant in Phnom Penh — French-Cambodian cuisine in a heritage setting
meals.dinner: Topaz Restaurant — French fine dining with Cambodian influences, exceptional wine cellar, and elegant colonial ambiance

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. These are critically important sites for understanding modern Cambodian history and should not be rushed. Photography is permitted in most areas with sensitivity.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the National Museum of Cambodia — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts spanning the pre-Angkor to post-Angkor periods. Followed by a walk through the riverside promenade (Sisowath Quay) and the French colonial quarter, admiring the architectural heritage of the former Indochine capital.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive visit to a premium Cambodian gem and jewelry workshop — Cambodia is renowned for rubies and sapphires from Pailin. Alternatively, visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for curated luxury shopping with a personal shopping guide. Afternoon river cruise on the Mekong aboard a private chartered boat.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class with a renowned Phnom Penh chef — learn to prepare three traditional Khmer dishes using market-fresh ingredients. Enjoy your creations as dinner with wine pairings in a private setting.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast — live cooking stations, international and Cambodian selections
meals.lunch: Rooftop lunch at Sora Restaurant (Rosewood) or Khéma Pasteur — light French-Asian fusion with Mekong views
meals.dinner: Private cooking class dinner experience — your own prepared Khmer feast with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum is closed on Mondays — Sunday timing is perfect. River cruises can be arranged through the hotel concierge with catering options. Cooking class venues include Frangipani Cooking Class or a private chef arrangement through the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Phnom Penh to Koh Rong Samloem or Kep/Kampot coastal region — approximately 3–4 hours by private car, or via chartered speedboat from Sihanoukville. Check in to a premium beachside resort such as Song Saa Private Island Resort (Koh Rong) or Knai Bang Chatt (Kep). Morning beach arrival and resort orientation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon of pure luxury beach relaxation — pristine white sand, turquoise Gulf of Thailand waters, and swaying palms. Private snorkeling excursion to nearby coral reefs teeming with tropical fish. Alternatively, a private kayaking tour through mangrove channels.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset on the private beach with champagne and canapés arranged by resort staff. Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant featuring the freshest Cambodian seafood — Kampot pepper crab, grilled lobster, and coconut-steamed clams.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Phnom Penh hotel before transfer
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at the resort — fresh ceviche, tropical salads, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — whole grilled sea bass, Kampot pepper crab, and lobster thermidor with chilled Sancerre

day_by_day.notes: November weather on Cambodia's coast is generally favorable — the Gulf of Thailand is calmer than the open ocean. Koh Rong Samloem offers bioluminescent plankton experiences at night — ask the resort about guided night swims. Song Saa Private Island requires advance booking well ahead of travel.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga session on the beach led by a resort instructor. Followed by a guided island exploration — hike through the jungle interior of the island to a secluded viewpoint or hidden cove. Alternatively, a private fishing excursion with local fishermen at dawn, catching your own breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulgent afternoon at the resort spa — 2-hour Cambodian royal treatment including a Khmer herbal steam bath, full-body coconut scrub, and a traditional four-hand massage. Followed by a private sunset sailing trip on a chartered traditional wooden boat around the island archipelago.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachside dinner under the stars — a bespoke menu created by the resort chef, served on a candlelit table on the sand with the sound of gentle waves. Bioluminescent plankton night swim experience (seasonal — November is excellent).

meals.breakfast: Fresh catch breakfast if fishing excursion taken — grilled fish, eggs, tropical fruits; otherwise full resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the resort — club sandwiches, fresh fruit smoothies, and Cambodian noodle soup
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner — five-course bespoke menu with freshly caught seafood, Kampot pepper sauces, and a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescent plankton are best viewed on nights with little moonlight — check lunar calendar. The spa should be booked 24 hours in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystems. The sailing excursion can be combined with a snorkeling stop.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — leisurely breakfast at the resort with panoramic ocean views. Last swim in the crystal-clear waters or a peaceful meditation session on the beach. Pack and check out with a fond farewell from resort staff. If time permits, a brief visit to a local fishing village for a final cultural encounter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer back to Phnom Penh or Siem Reap airport (depending on departure flight routing). En route, if passing through Kampot, stop for a brief visit to the famous Kampot pepper farms — tour the plantation and purchase premium Kampot pepper (a world-renowned spice) as a luxury souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia — airport lounge access arranged. Final reflections on an extraordinary 10-day journey through the Kingdom of Wonder — from the ancient temples of Angkor to the pristine beaches of the Gulf of Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Lavish final resort breakfast — eggs your way, pastries, tropical fruits, Cambodian congee, and freshly brewed Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch in Kampot at Rikitikitavi or Epic Arts Café — riverside setting with fresh Cambodian cuisine and Kampot pepper dishes
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal (departure dependent)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 4–5 hours for the coastal-to-airport transfer. Kampot pepper farms offer retail purchase of premium red, black, and white pepper — excellent luxury gifts. Confirm return transfer and flight check-in times with the hotel concierge the evening before. Duty-free at Phnom Penh or Siem Reap airports offers Cambodian rum, silk, and handicrafts.
